newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Kinkel tells Slovakia NATO door still open.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel tells Slovakia NATO door still open.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel assured Slovakia on Friday that if it were left out of the first round of NATO expansion it would not be totally excluded from the alliance.
"There are no fixed candidates for the first round of NATO expansion when the alliance meets in July in Madrid," Kinkel told a news conference in Bratislava at the end of a two-day visit to Slovakia.
"But failure to be invited among the first candidates for expansion in no way means that the door to NATO is shut. There is no closed door policy," Kinkel added.
Slovakia has repeatedly declared its priority and desire to to be among the first countries invited by NATO to join the alliance after its summit in Madrid in July.
But its chances appear to have waned in recent months after repeated U.S. and European Union criticism, including that of Germany, over the pace of its democratic reforms.
Rita Suessmuth, the President of the German Bundestag said earlier this year that Slovakia had a 'deficit in democracy' which was a barrier to early membership of NATO and the European Union.
Kinkel said deficiencies in Slovakia's political and economic reforms, including privatisation, were also a barrier to bigger German investments in the Slovak economy.
"The framework for investments must be improved," Kinkel said. "Money goes where it expects good conditions."
Slovak Foreign Minister Pavolo Hamzik said trade with Germany last year was worth six billion marks with a slight Slovak surplus.
